description: This donut chart, titled “Distribution of deceived conversations (%) across varying degrees of ambiguity,” visually compares the proportion of deceived conversations under two distinct ambiguity conditions: “Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner).” The chart is composed of two concentric rings, each divided into three colored segments representing the categories “Deceived” (red), “Partially” (yellow), and “Not Deceived” (green), with corresponding legends provided for each ring. The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity 1 (Outer),” shows the following proportions: the red “Deceived” segment accounts for 67.6%, the yellow “Partially” segment for 57.9%, and the green “Not Deceived” segment for 31.6%. The inner ring, labeled “Ambiguity 2 (Inner),” displays: the red “Deceived” segment at 10.5%, the yellow “Partially” segment at 23.5%, and the green “Not Deceived” segment at 8.8%. Each segment is clearly labeled with its percentage value, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise order, with the largest segment (red) positioned at the top of each ring. The chart includes two separate legends, one for each ring, explicitly mapping the color to the category.
